title: Latency Topography & Token Ripples — Per-Route Performance Canvas Spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a compact, scannable per-route performance canvas that surfaces distributional latency signals and token-level variability without requiring users to open full traces. The design explores two novel metaphors: a 'latency topography' contour map (shows latency as elevation across percentile and time dimensions) and 'token ripples' sparklines (small multiples showing token-level variance across recent requests). This ticket captures the UI spec, interaction patterns, prototype frames, and review feedback for handoff to frontend and data infra.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype frames in Figma for both collapsed tile and expanded canvas states
Chart specs (data schema, axes, tooltip payload) documented and agreed with infra/eng
Behavior definitions for canary vs baseline comparisons and color semantics
Design review sign-off from PM (Sarah Li) and Eng lead (Ravi Menon)
Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard expansion controls verified
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- Tile defaults to a 280x120 compact card: left column shows a micro-contour (latency topography) rendered as 16x64 grid; right column stacks two micro-sparklines: TPS (throughput) and Token Ripples (token variance).
- Expanded canvas (modal or route panel) replaces micro-contour with interactive topography: X axis = time window (last 60m), Y axis = latency percentiles (50/90/95/99) rendered as stacked contour bands. Hover reveals request examples and small raw-token histograms.
- Token Ripples: encode per-token latency variance with radial ripples per token position where ripple amplitude = stddev(ms) and color = median latency bucket. This compresses 512 token positions into small multiples with truncation controls.
- Interaction: keyboard focus moves between tiles; Enter expands; hover previews sample log lines; click sample opens trace in traces explorer.
- Data sampling: default uses reservoir sampling of 500 requests per route for last 60m. UI shows sampling badge and link to source query.
- Controls: time window selector, baseline toggle (compare vs previous window or vs model variant), percentile picker, and quantization level (raw vs binned).
decisions: Use contour/topography metaphor rather than heatmap to emphasize distributional 'shape' over absolute color intensity
Token ripples prioritized for routes where median token counts > 64; otherwise show compact token heatline
Default color palette follows Console brand but with distinct high-latency accent (deep cinnabar) to avoid green-red confusion for colorblind users
tradeoffs:
- Contour rendering is heavier on client-side; we agreed to precompute contour bands server-side for common windows to keep interactive perf acceptable.
- Token ripples are visually novel but can be noisy; included an option to fall back to token-mean/median line charts when variance is low.
- Sampling introduces potential missing spikes; added an explicit sampling indicator and 'live capture' CTA for on-demand full traces.
review_comments:
Design review 2026-02-22:
- PM (Sarah Li): 'Love the topography metaphor — helps call out mode shifts. Need clearer CTA to open traces and to pin baseline comparisons.'
- Eng (Ravi Menon): 'Compute needs: pre-binning contour bands + sampled token variance. Request infra to add a 2s SLA for contour payloads; otherwise consider progressive loading.'
- Research (Ellen Cho): 'User tests show developers interpret contour peaks as incidents; add explicit annotations for three most recent unusual peaks and link them to incidents if present.'
- Accessibility (Marco Alvarez): 'Ensure ripple glyphs have text alternatives and keyboard focus traps. Provide color-defensive textures option.'
Progress updates:
- 2026-02-25: Prototype v1 uploaded to Figma and demoed to Console team (embedding: figma link below).
- 2026-02-27: Updated chart spec with eng feedback to include precomputed bands and sampling metadata.
- 2026-03-01: Locked tile sizing and responsive rules; moved to In Review for cross-team sign-off.
